svg.title: Focus Stacking with the Laplacian Pyramid
svg.desc: Step-by-step infographic: a stack of shallow depth-of-field frames is decomposed into Laplacian bands, scored by local focus energy, merged band by band, and collapsed back into one fully sharp image.

g.text: Focus Stacking with the Laplacian Pyramid
Burt & Adelson (1983) decomposition · energy-weighted band selection · one all-in-focus render
Each frame is taken at a different focus distance. At macro magnification only a thin slab of the subject resolves.
Why one exposure is not enough
Depth of field shrinks with magnification. At 1:1
and f/8 it can fall below a millimetre, so no single
aperture renders the whole subject — stopping
down further trades focus for diffraction blur.
Solution: fuse many frames, not one.
Every frame is split into scales: repeated 2×-downsampling gives a Gaussian pyramid; each band is what one level loses to the next.
The pyramid is lossless — and that is the point
The bands add back exactly to the original image, so anything decided
band by band can be reassembled without inventing pixels.
Each band answers a different question:
L₀–L₁ — pore-level texture, grain, the finest hairs
L₂–L₃ — contours, structural edges, coarse relief
G₄ base — overall tone and colour, no detail at all
Working across scales is what stops a single sharp speck from dragging a whole region with it.
Measure focus — local energy per band
A single |Laplacian| pixel is noise. Pooling its square over a 5×5 window turns it into a region measure: a focus heatmap per frame, per band.
no detail resolved — defocus, flat tone, grain only
high band energy — genuinely in focus
Dividing by nᵢ, the frame's own noise level (10th percentile of
its live band energies), stops a bright defocused veil from
outscoring a dark sharp frame on grain alone. Every frame then
reads about 1.0 where it resolves nothing — so those regions tie.
Select & merge — band by band, pixel by pixel
The classic rule copies the strongest coefficient. A soft exponent keeps that decision where it is real and averages where nothing is in focus.
wᵢ = ( eᵢ / e_max ) ^ β with β = 8
A frame 2× behind the winner contributes 2⁻⁸ ≈ 0.4 % — effectively a decision, without the speckle.
Boundaries follow depth, not a grid.
Where frames tie, the weights average them —
the correct answer for “nothing resolves here”.
Collapse the pyramid — one fully focused image
From the coarsest level down: upsample, add the fused band, repeat. The stack is gone; the detail of every frame is not.
Fᵢ = L̂ᵢ + pyrUp(Fᵢ₊₁) — coarsest level first, fused band added at every scale
Front to back sharp — from a stack no single exposure could capture.
Burt P. J., Adelson E. H. — “The Laplacian pyramid as a compact image code”, IEEE Trans. Communications 31(4), 1983.
